items.requirement: tsrs checks and emits TSX (react-jsx) against virtual node_modules declarations for React and a custom SDK package, from an in-memory file map
evidence: Node run of @tsrs/wasm 0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta, 2026-11-10: exit 0 on a valid file, TS2339 and TS2345 on the planted errors, about 260 ms cold, 111 MiB. Not yet run in a browser worker.

items.requirement: A rustyred-wasm crate in RustyRedDB builds the graph store over the OPFS projection chunk store and over memory, without Database::create/open
evidence: RustyRedDB PR #4 (feat/browser-binding, f873b62): Database::with_chunk_store and crates/rustyred-wasm
cargo test -p rustyred-wasm: 4 passed; cargo test -p rustyred --test chunk_store_database: 2 passed

items.requirement: @rustyreddb/browser mirrors the Node binding (mutate, getNode, getEdge, queryNodes, neighbors, query, fulltext, compact, close) with the same error codes, behind an async client that owns the worker
evidence: RustyRedDB PR #4 (feat/browser-binding, f873b62): crates/rustyred-wasm/npm (worker.js, index.js, index.d.ts)
Not included: designateFulltext and fulltextSearch (Tantivy default features do not build for wasm32; the call answers fulltext_unavailable) and compact (native .RR files only)

items.requirement: subscribe re-runs a registered read after a commit and posts the result
evidence: RustyRedDB PR #4 (feat/browser-binding, f873b62): npm/src/worker.js publish(); oracle check "a subscription sees each change to its read and nothing else"
Every subscribed read is run again after each commit and reported only when its result differs

items.requirement: Headless Chromium: records written are read back after a page reload; runtime panics on wasm32 found by this run are fixed
evidence: npm run oracle in headless Chromium, 2026-11-10: 14 of 14 checks; records, edge and graph version present after a page reload; verify ok before and after
No wasm32 runtime panic appeared on these paths. Module 3.9 MB; first open about 90 ms, open after reload about 160 ms
2026-11-10, later: 21 of 21 checks with the shared mode, five runs

items.requirement: A db capability is declared like the others and db.* page methods are parsed and checked against it
evidence: src/lib/blocks/declarations.ts (db), bridge.ts (db.call, db.subscribe, db.unsubscribe, each zod-parsed and checked against the declaration)
bun test src/lib/blocks/app-db.test.ts: 13 passed, including "a database that was not declared is not reached"

items.requirement: One database per App document id in a host-page worker; every revision of an App sees the same records; a pinned revision is read-only
evidence: src/lib/blocks/app-db.ts: one database per App document id and declared name, shared by every view on the page; a pinned revision is opened with writable false

node scripts/e2e/app-db.mjs in headless Chromium, 2026-11-10: 9 of 9 checks, including "the next revision of the App finds its records", "they are there after the page is loaded again" and "a saved revision reads them and may not change them"

items.requirement: Two tabs showing the same App share its database: one tab owns the worker and the others reach it, because OPFS gives one exclusive handle per file
evidence: RustyRedDB PR #4: open(name, { shared: true }) in crates/rustyred-wasm/npm/src/shared.js (a Web Lock chooses the tab that holds the file, a BroadcastChannel carries the others' calls); its oracle drives three pages, 21 of 21 checks
src/lib/blocks/app-db.ts opens shared; bun run e2e:app-db: "a write in one tab reaches the other" and "the App keeps working in the tab that is left", 14 of 14 checks, three runs

items.requirement: An App's database does not grow without bound: the browser store is compacted
evidence: Not built. The engine's browser store refuses reclamation by design (rustyred-engine browser_projection.rs, chunk_store_browser_compaction_refused): OPFS has no atomic rename, and the route it names is a two-file generation switch

Measured in headless Chromium, 2026-11-10, 200 small nodes then 1000 one-node commits: the file grew about 7 KB per commit as Theorem UI opens it (controlEvents and keepHistory off), 7 MB in all, at about 33 ms per commit; with both on, about 100 KB and 100 ms per commit

bun run e2e:app-db: "the calls Theorem's builder is told to use work as it is told"

items.requirement: tsrs checks the same frozen snapshot in its own worker, loaded on first use; results for a superseded revision are dropped
evidence: src/lib/blocks/app-check.ts, app-check.worker.ts, app-checker.ts (one lazy worker for the page; checks run one after another); document-app.tsx useTypeCheck drops a result for another revision
bun test src/lib/blocks/app-check.test.ts: 5 passed against tsrs's Node build
bun run e2e:app-ts: the worker reports TS2339 and TS2322 at their file and line; a check took about 100 to 140 ms and 111 MiB once loaded

app-check.test.ts: "the declarations for window.theorem are the ones its source gives" fails when the generated file is stale; "a call the bridge does not have, or a wrong argument to one it has, is a problem"

items.requirement: Checker load, memory and time measured on a phone
evidence: Measured in headless desktop Chromium only: the tsrs module is 10 MB (1.7 MB brotli), a check of a three-file React App about 100 to 140 ms and 111 MiB once loaded. No phone was measured.

items.requirement: Each rendered element names the file, line and column that wrote it, added at build time and never written into source; a selection carries it to the agent
evidence: src/lib/blocks/export.ts: the App's JSX runtime stamps data-theorem-source from the place esbuild passes to jsxDEV, so no index is kept and no source is parsed
sandbox/app-bridge.ts sends the nearest one as selection.source; app-references.ts labels the reference by file and line
bun run e2e:app-ts, dev and --built: "an element says where it was written, and pointing at it tells the agent" (Table.tsx:26:13)

items.requirement: Reversible actions (property, token or style, insert, reorder, remove, binding, extract) become AST edits against the revision they were made on
evidence: Built: set an element's plain text, and set, add or remove an attribute written as a string (src/lib/blocks/app-edit.ts editElement, writeAppSource; src/components/blocks/app-element.tsx). Each is a new App revision, so the revision history is the undo
bun test src/lib/blocks/app-edit.test.ts: 12 passed; typescript-app.test.tsx: "pointing at an element offers its plain text and attributes, and applying rewrites its source"
bun run e2e:app-ts, dev and --built: "changing an element in the panel rewrites its source, and the App shows it"
Not built: insert into a slot, reorder, remove, change a binding, extract a component, token and style edits, and any edit to a value written as code
